docs.title: Icons
docs.text: Plugins can ship PNG icons for Car rows, page items and status items. The HMI draws them; you never draw graphics yourself.

docs.title: Declare icons
docs.text:
Add the names to plugin.json:

{
  "api": 3,
  "icons": ["cup", "cup-20"]
}

Put the files at src/main/icons/<name>.png. Names match [a-z0-9-]{1,32}; a plugin may declare at most 8.

The build fails if a declared file is missing or does not pass the PNG rules. mibpkgPackage also stages a faded reflection <name>.r.png for every icon taller than 20 px; the Car drawer draws it under the row icon. You do not create the reflection yourself.

docs.title: PNG rules
docs.text:
Rule Value Format 8-bit RGBA, or 8-bit grey + alpha. Not palette, not 16-bit Interlacing None Animation None Maximum size 72 px either way Maximum file size 32 KiB

White glyphs on transparent backgrounds look like the stock icons. The Car drawer draws row icons in their own colours, so a white glyph is the stock look.

docs.title: Sizes by use
docs.text:
Use API Maximum Notes Car row ui.carMenuRow(label, page, icon) 72×72 (Ui.ROW_ICON_MAX_PX) Own colours Status item, toast ui.statusItem(text, icon), ui.toast(text, icon) 20×20 (StatusItem.ICON_MAX_PX) Tinted by default; Icon.OWN_COLOURS keeps the PNG colours Page item PageSpec.item(id, label, value, icon) 24×24 (PageSpec.ITEM_ICON_MAX_PX) The cell does not scale Built-in ui.stockIcon(...) — No file

The size check is per use, at runtime. A 72 px icon passed to statusItem builds and packages, then throws IllegalArgumentException when the plugin runs. Ship a small icon for the status line:

src/main/icons/cup.png       72×72   Car row
src/main/icons/cup-20.png    20×20   status item and toast

permissionScan warns when a call names an oversized icon literally, but only for a literal ui.icon("name"); a field or a local is not judged.

docs.title: Getting an icon
docs.text:
Icon cup = ctx.ui().icon("cup");                    // tinted, the default
Icon own = ctx.ui().icon("logo", Icon.OWN_COLOURS); // keep the PNG colours
Icon star = ctx.ui().stockIcon(StockIcons.STAR);
  • An undeclared name throws IllegalArgumentException.
  • An icon from another plugin (or a hand-made implementation) is rejected.
  • An icon declared but not installed — for example after a jar push without a package — is inert: rows and items show without it, and the runtime logs one WARN.
  • Icons are static per installed package version. A new picture needs a new package.

docs.title: Tinted or own colours
docs.text:
Icon.TINTED (the default) draws the icon in the app colour, like the stock icons. Icon.OWN_COLOURS keeps the PNG's colours.

  • Status items and toasts honour the flag.
  • Car rows ignore it: the drawer always draws row icons in their own colours.
  • Built-in icons are always tinted; they are white glyphs.

docs.title: Built-in icons
docs.text:
StockIcons provides DOT, CIRCLE, STAR, TRIANGLE, SQUARE, CHECK, CROSS and PLUG. They need no file and are always small enough for any use.

ctx.ui().carMenuRow("Plugins", page, ctx.ui().stockIcon(StockIcons.PLUG));

docs.title: Generating icons
docs.text:
The tutorial's generator writes 8-bit RGBA PNGs with the standard library:

python3 plugins/coffee-timer/make_icons.py src/main/icons

Any image editor that exports 8-bit RGBA works. Keep the two right-most columns of a 20 px status icon clear: the status text starts right after the icon cell.

docs.title: Networking
docs.text: Plugins can talk to services on the unit, and — with an extra permission — to hosts outside it. The API is plain TCP; there is no HTTP client and no TLS stack on the car.

docs.title: Query a service
docs.text:
if (ctx.granted(Permissions.NETWORK)) {
    try {
        String reply = ctx.net().query("127.0.0.1", 8080, "status", 1000);
        ctx.log().info("daemon says " + reply);
    } catch (IOException e) {
        ctx.log().warn("daemon did not answer: " + e.getMessage());
    }
}
Rule Value Loopback 127.0.0.1 or localhost, with network Remote host Any host name or IP, with network and network.outbound Request At most 2048 UTF-8 bytes; a newline is appended Response At most 8192 bytes, read to EOF Timeout At most 3000 ms, including DNS resolution Transport Plain TCP. No TLS

Any port is reachable. A request longer than 2048 bytes throws IOException. A server that keeps the connection open after sending 8 KiB or more produces a SocketTimeoutException rather than a truncated result, because the read runs to EOF.

docs.title: Reaching outside the unit
docs.text:
Outbound access is a second, separately approved permission:

"permissions": ["network", "network.outbound"]

String reply = ctx.net().query("api.example.com", 80, "GET /status HTTP/1.0\r\nHost: api.example.com\r\n", 2000);

The unit has no TLS stack (javax.net.ssl is not in its class library), so https:// is not available from a plugin. Options:

  • use a plain-HTTP endpoint on your own network;
  • run a small local proxy on the unit that terminates TLS and expose it on loopback;
  • keep the plugin on loopback and let another process do the outbound request.

The SDK does not ship an HTTP client. If you need one, build the request string yourself, or add a local daemon that speaks a simple protocol.

docs.title: Wi-Fi uplink
docs.text:
The SDK itself owns the car's internet uplink. The user sets a phone hotspot from Plugins → SDK → Internet on the car, or from More → Internet in mibpkg's web UI. Both edit the same file, /mnt/persist/mibsdk/wifi.toml, and the SDK applies a change within a second. The same page chooses DHCP (the default) or a manual IPv4 address, netmask, gateway and optional DNS servers. The SDK runs the stock dhcp.client itself when the interface has no address, so a reboot does not need a manual DHCP kick. With DHCP on, the Internet page also shows the live IP, netmask, gateway and DNS from the lease. The car's own access point stays up while the client is connected: the stock Wi-Fi service runs the access point and the client together. There is no SIM requirement and no extra daemon.

A plugin can use the same uplink with ctx.wifi() and the network.wifi permission:

if (ctx.has(Features.WIFI)) {
    WifiStatus s = ctx.wifi().status();
    if (!s.connected()) {
        for (WifiNetwork n : ctx.wifi().scan(5000)) {
            ctx.log().info(n.ssid() + " " + n.signal() + "% " + n.encryption());
        }
    }
}
Call Meaning status() The last state, SSID, IPv4, signal and error scan(ms) A blocking scan; the result is strongest first connect(ssid, password) Join a network; the result arrives as WifiChanged disconnect() Leave the current network forget(ssid) Remove a saved network onChanged(listener) State changes on the plugin's worker

connect and disconnect return at once. A password may be null or empty for an open network. Wi-Fi scan and connect are the only blocking calls; keep the timeout short on the worker. The API does not expose radio settings, the access point, or WPS.

wifi.toml also takes dhcp = false with ip, netmask, gateway and dns; the car page and the web page edit the same fields. The SDK's own page and this API never print the saved password. mibpkg's web page returns only whether one is set.

docs.title: Poll a daemon on a schedule
docs.text:
Subscription poll = ctx.scheduler().every(30_000, () -> {
    try {
        String state = ctx.net().query("127.0.0.1", 8099, "tailscale status", 1000);
        status.set(state);
    } catch (IOException e) {
        status.set("offline");
    }
});

every runs on the plugin's worker thread. A poll still delays other callbacks, so keep the timeout short and do not overlap polls.

docs.title: Query once on start
docs.text:
ctx.scheduler().after(0, () -> {
    try {
        String version = ctx.net().query("127.0.0.1", 8099, "version", 500);
        ctx.log().info("daemon " + version.trim());
    } catch (IOException e) {
        ctx.log().warn("daemon unavailable");
    }
});

docs.title: What you cannot do
docs.text:
• Open a listening socket.
  • Use java.net.Socket, ServerSocket, URL.openConnection or InetAddress.getByName directly. The build rejects them unless you declare platform.unrestricted.
  • Use https:// or any TLS API. The car has no JSSE.
  • Use an HTTP client library; it is not on the car's class library.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
Permission Approval text network Query local services on this unit (loopback only) network.outbound Connect to hosts outside this unit network.wifi Use the Wi-Fi client uplink to connect to a phone hotspot or another network

A plugin that declares a permission but is not granted it is BLOCKED_PERMISSIONS and does not start. A plugin with network but without network.outbound can still use loopback; a remote call throws PermissionDeniedException naming network.outbound.

The build cannot tell which host a call will use, so it checks only network at build time. Declare network.outbound when you use a non-loopback host.

docs.title: Pages and inputs
docs.text:
A plugin page is a declarative PageSpec: a title and a list of rows. The runtime draws it with the HMI's own cells, checkboxes, sliders, dropdowns and dialogs. You never draw anything yourself.

Page page = ctx.ui().page(
        PageSpec.of("main", "My plugin")
                .item("status", "Status", "Idle")
                .toggle("enabled", "Enabled", true)
                .info("Changes are saved automatically."),
        action -> handle(action));

ui.page also lists the page under your plugin's entry in the Plugins menu. To put it in the Car drawer:

ctx.ui().carMenuRow("My plugin", page, ctx.ui().stockIcon(StockIcons.STAR));

A plugin may have at most 8 pages and 2 Car rows. See Limits.

docs.title: Page and item ids
docs.text:
• Page ids and item ids match [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,32}.
  • Item ids are unique within a page.
  • A page's key for the test harness and the menu is <plugin id>/<page id>.

An invalid id throws IllegalArgumentException.

docs.title: Rows
docs.text:
Builder Draws Action item(id, label, value) A list row with a value column select item(id, label, value, icon) The same with a 24 px icon select toggle(id, label, on) The native checkbox requestedOn() info(text) A text line none link(id, label, target) A row that opens another page select choice(id, label, options, selected) A list row that opens an option list value() = index dropdown(id, label, options, selected) An inline drop-down value() = index slider(id, label, min, max, step, value, centred) A slider on its own screen value() = level progress(id, label, percent) A progress bar none

Text is never rejected for length; the runtime truncates it. Counts are enforced: a 25th entry throws IllegalStateException.

docs.title: Toggles
docs.text:
A toggle does not flip by itself. The HMI sends the requested state and keeps showing what your next update says:

private void onAction(UiAction a) {
    if ("enabled".equals(a.itemId())) {
        enabled = a.requestedOn().booleanValue();
        storage.put("enabled", enabled ? "on" : "off");
        page.update(spec());
    }
}

docs.title: Sliders
docs.text:
PageSpec.of("main", "Lights")
        .slider("brightness", "Brightness", 0, 100, 10, brightness, false)

Rules: min < max, step >= 1, (max - min) % step == 0, at most 24 steps, and the current value on the grid. A centred slider (drawn from the middle, like a balance) needs an even step count. A page may have at most 4 dropdown plus slider rows; they are drawn after the list rows.

A slider shows its position, not its number. If the number matters, show it in another row's value column.

docs.title: Choice and dropdown
docs.text:
String[] modes = {"Eco", "Comfort", "Sport"};
PageSpec.of("main", "Drive mode")
        .choice("mode", "Mode", modes, mode)
        .dropdown("fan", "Fan", new String[] {"Low", "Mid", "High"}, fan);

The pick arrives as value(), the index into your options array. choice opens a sub-page; its key is <pageKey>#<itemId> and its option ids are "0", "1", ... The test harness's choose(...) opens it for you.

docs.title: Disabled rows
docs.text:
spec = spec.enabled("stop", false);

Only ITEM, TOGGLE, LINK and CHOICE rows can be disabled. A disabled row is greyed and cannot be selected. Any other kind throws.

docs.title: Progress
docs.text:
spec = spec.progress("copy", "Copying", percent);

percent is clamped to 0..100. Progress is display-only.

docs.title: Handling actions
docs.text:
private void onAction(UiAction a) {
    switch (a.itemId()) {
        case "start" -> start();
        case "stop" -> stop();
        case "brightness" -> {
            brightness = a.value().intValue();
            storage.put("brightness", String.valueOf(brightness));
        }
        default -> log.warn("unknown item " + a.itemId());
    }
    page.update(spec());
}

UiAction gives you:

Method Value pageId() The page itemId() The row requestedOn() The requested checkbox state; null for other rows value() Option index, slider level, or 1/0 for confirm; null otherwise text() Speller text; null otherwise

Actions arrive on the plugin's worker thread, one at a time. Rebuild the whole spec from your fields and call page.update(spec); that is the pattern every sample uses.

docs.title: Dialogs
docs.text: Dialogs need api 5 and Features.UI_INPUTS. They open only while one of your pages is the open page.

docs.title: Confirm
docs.text:
ctx.ui().confirm("Stop the timer?", "The brew will be lost.", "Stop", "Keep brewing", answer -> {
    if (answer.value().intValue() == 1) {
        stop();
    }
});
  • At most 3 lines and 120 characters.
  • value() is 1 for Yes and 0 for No, BACK, dismissed, or a dialog that could not be shown.
  • The listener is called exactly once unless you cancel the returned Subscription first.

docs.title: Toast
docs.text:
ctx.ui().toast("Coffee is ready", cupSmall);
  • 20 characters, optional 20 px icon, 3 seconds.
  • Needs ui.slot.statusbar; without it, PermissionDeniedException.
  • Inert without Features.UI_INPUTS.

docs.title: Speller (experimental)
docs.text:
ctx.ui().speller("Name", initial, 32, done -> {
    String text = done.text(); // null if the speller never showed
});

The HMI speller has no OK key: BACK leaves it and counts as done. text() is null when the speller never showed or was dismissed because its page closed.

docs.title: Missing features
docs.text: When the unit cannot draw the UI this boot, page, carMenuRow, statusItem, toast, confirm and speller still return handles, but they are inert. Argument and count checks still apply. Check ctx.has(Features.UI_PAGES) or Features.UI_INPUTS when the difference matters.

docs.title: Package and publish a plugin
docs.text: A plugin is distributed as a mibpkg package (.mpk). You can share it with a file, a release, or a package index; there is no central registry.

docs.title: Build the jar
docs.text:
./gradlew mibPluginJar

build/mibsdk/<id>.jar
build/mibsdk/<id>.jar.stamp

The jar contains the backported classes and plugin.json. The stamp records the checks that ran and the jar's SHA-256. mibpkg refuses a jar without a valid stamp, so do not edit the jar after the build.

docs.title: Build the package
docs.text:
./gradlew mibpkgPackage -Pmibsdk.mibpkg=/path/to/mibpkg

build/mibsdk/<id>-<version>.mpk

The package contains:

  • the stamped jar;
  • the icons from src/main/icons/, plus a generated <name>.r.png reflection for each icon taller than 20 px;
  • a generated manifest.toml with the id, version, unit compatibility, api level, permissions and icons.

The staged files are in build/mibpkg-stage/. The task is mibpkgPackage; mibPackage is a deprecated alias.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text:
The plugin's version is semver in plugin.json:

{ "version": "1.2.3" }

mibpkg uses it to order updates. Raise it for every release you publish. Pre-release tags such as 1.2.3-beta.1 are accepted.

The "api" field is different from the version: it is the newest plugin API your code uses. See API levels.

docs.title: Install and approve
docs.text:
mibpkg shows the plugin's permissions in plain words and installs only after approval:

  • Web interface: upload the .mpk and accept the sheet.
  • CLI: mibpkg install-file <id> ...; exits 3 until you re-run with --approve=<perm,...>.

Installing writes:

  • plugins/<id>.jar;
  • icons/<id>/<sha16>.png and index.properties;
  • a line in grants.properties.

The running SDK loads the plugin within a few seconds; no HMI restart is needed.

docs.title: Updating
docs.text:
Build a new .mpk with a higher version and install it. mibpkg replaces the jar, icons and grants. If the new version needs a new permission, the approval sheet shows only the new permission.

A jar push during development is faster but carries no icons and no permissions. Once you are happy, install the package so the unit has the full set.

docs.title: Removing
docs.text:
installer/mibsdk-dev remove coffee-timer <unit-ip>            # keep storage
installer/mibsdk-dev remove coffee-timer --purge <unit-ip>    # remove storage too

Removing a plugin releases its vehicle overrides and cancels its registrations. Its storage stays unless you purge it.

docs.title: Sharing
docs.text:
A plugin repository should contain:

  • the source;
  • the Gradle wrapper;
  • a README.md with what the plugin does, its permissions and how to install it;
  • a license;
  • optionally, the built .mpk as a release asset.

Do not commit build/, .gradle/ or machine-specific mibsdk.repo values.

docs.title: Status line and toasts
docs.text: A plugin can add one short item to the car's status line and show toasts at the top of the screen. Both need the ui.slot.statusbar permission.

docs.title: A status item
docs.text:
StatusItem status = ctx.ui().statusItem("Coffee 4m", ctx.ui().icon("cup-20"));
...
status.set("Coffee 3m");
status.set(null); // hide
Rule Value Items per plugin 1 Text 12 characters, truncated Icon 20×20 px, optional Permission ui.slot.statusbar

set(null) or set("") hides the item. The item is not an error if the user hides it: the user can reorder or hide items from the SDK's page in the Plugins menu, and set keeps working.

docs.title: Icons
docs.text:
Icon cup = ctx.ui().icon("cup-20");            // tinted in the app colour
Icon logo = ctx.ui().icon("logo-20", Icon.OWN_COLOURS);
Icon star = ctx.ui().stockIcon(StockIcons.STAR);
  • A plug-in icon is declared in plugin.json and lives at src/main/icons/<name>.png.
  • Status icons are at most 20×20 px; a larger one throws IllegalArgumentException.
  • The icon must come from this plugin's Ui.
  • Built-in icons need no file.

docs.title: Icon-only items
docs.text:
status.setIcon(ctx.ui().icon("cup-20"));
status.setIcon(null); // hide

An icon-only item gets a fixed slot in the bar's left strip, so several plugin icons can be visible at once. Calling set(text) goes back to a text item.

docs.title: Colour
docs.text:
status.setColour(UiColor.rgb(255, 180, 0));
status.setColour(null); // the bar's own colour

A colour is global: it applies in every HMI context and does not follow the palette. Only the text takes it; icons keep their own colour rules. In the popup fallback (where the built-in bar is unavailable) the text keeps the popup's colour.

docs.title: Per-screen visibility
docs.text:
status.visibleIn(HmiContext.CAR);
status.visibleIn(HmiContext.CAR, HmiContext.MEDIA);
status.visibleIn(); // every context, the default

Contexts are the stock status bar's contexts: CAR, TUNER, MEDIA, PHONE, NAVI, MAP, ONLINE, OFFICE, TONE, SETTINGS. HmiContext.NONE is not a context and is rejected.

The built-in bar applies the limit. The popup fallback shows every item.

docs.title: How the line is shared
docs.text:
The line is shared with the SDK's own indicators and other plugins:

  • Safety indicators (SAFE, PDC R OFF) always show.
  • Plugin items share the remaining width fairly, in the user's order, then plugin id.
  • An item shorter than its share shows whole; a longer one may be cut with ....
  • When even three characters each do not fit, the last items are left out.

Put the important part first. "Coffee ready" is exactly 12 characters.

docs.title: Toasts
docs.text:
ctx.ui().toast("Coffee is ready", cupSmall);
Rule Value Text 20 characters, truncated Icon 20×20 px, optional Duration 3 seconds Permission ui.slot.statusbar Feature Features.UI_INPUTS; inert without it

A toast does not queue: a new toast replaces the previous one. It shows at the top of the screen and disappears on its own.

docs.title: The SDK's status-bar settings
docs.text: The SDK's entry in the Plugins menu holds the built-in bar's settings: on/off, dwell time (default 5 s), animation (default 300 ms) and the global item order. They are stored in /mnt/persist/mibsdk/statusbar.properties. A plugin cannot read or change them.

docs.title: Missing features
docs.text: Without Features.SLOT_STATUS_BAR the item and the toast are inert. Without Features.UI_ICONS they show without icons, but the icon size and ownership checks still apply.

docs.title: Storage and timers
docs.text: Plugins get a small persistent key/value store and a scheduler that runs work on the plugin's own worker thread. Both are cancelled or flushed automatically when the plugin is disabled.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
Storage storage = ctx.storage();

String minutes = storage.get("minutes", "4");
storage.put("minutes", "7");
storage.remove("minutes");
Rule Value Type String keys and string values, per plugin Persistence Survives reboots Per-plugin cap 256 KiB by default All-plugins cap 1 MiB by default Location /mnt/persist/mibsdk/data/<id>.properties

A put that would exceed a cap throws IllegalStateException and stores nothing. Removing keys or storing shorter values always works. The caps are set in sdk.properties on the unit.

Storage is written shortly after a put and on shutdown. It is shared with the stock persistence partition, so keep data small.

docs.title: Parse defensively
docs.text:
Stored values can come from an older version of your plugin, or be missing:

private int storedMinutes() {
    try {
        int m = Integer.parseInt(storage.get("minutes", "4"));
        return m >= 1 && m <= 10 ? m : 4;
    } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
        return 4;
    }
}

Do not assume a key exists, and do not assume its value is valid.

docs.title: Scheduler
docs.text:
Scheduler scheduler = ctx.scheduler();

Subscription once = scheduler.after(5_000, () -> ctx.log().info("five seconds later"));
Subscription tick = scheduler.every(60_000, this::onMinute);
tick.cancel();
Method Behaviour after(delayMs, task) Runs once, no sooner than delayMs from now. A negative delay counts as 0 every(periodMs, task) Runs every periodMs, starting one period from now
  • periodMs must be at least 1.
  • A run that comes due while the previous one is still queued is skipped, not piled up, so a slow task does not produce a burst of catch-up runs.
  • Cancelling twice is harmless.
  • Everything scheduled is cancelled when the plugin is disabled, quarantined or reloaded.

docs.title: One worker, one task at a time
docs.text:
after and every tasks run on the plugin's single worker thread, like every other callback. They never overlap onEnable, page actions, event listeners or another task, and they never run on an HMI thread.

That means a slow task delays the rest of your plugin. The SDK logs a callback over 5 s as slow and quarantines a callback that runs for 30 s. Keep tasks short; use ctx.net() for bounded I/O (3 s timeout).

Do not start your own Thread for scheduled work. The SDK cannot cancel or quarantine it, and it will still be running after the plugin is disabled.

docs.title: Testing storage and timers
docs.text:
Properties before = new Properties();
before.setProperty("minutes", "2");
PluginTestHarness h = PluginTestHarness.builder(tmp).storedValues(before).start();

h.ui().select(h.pageKey("timer"), "start");
h.advance(60_000);                    // move the scheduler forward
h.await(() -> "Coffee 1m".equals(h.ui().statusLine()), "one minute");

Properties after = h.storedValues(); // stops the runtime and flushes storage
assertEquals("2", after.getProperty("minutes"));

h.restart() stops and starts on the same directory, keeping storage, so you can test that values come back. Call h.ui() again after a restart.

docs.title: Vehicle and events
docs.text: Vehicle access is deliberately narrow: read the parking-sound state, change it with a permission, and observe a few vehicle events. Anything deeper belongs in a firmware adapter, not a plugin.

docs.title: Reading parking state
docs.text:
if (ctx.has(Features.PARKING)) {
    SoundDirections now = ctx.vehicle().parking().soundDirections();
    boolean rear = now.rear();
}

SoundDirections is immutable and has front(), rear(), left(), right() and withRear(...).

ctx.vehicle() needs the vehicle.read permission. Without Features.PARKING the parking system is not available and the call throws UnsupportedOperationException; check ctx.has(...) first.

docs.title: Overriding parking sound
docs.text:
VehicleOverride override = null;

try {
    override = ctx.vehicle().parking().overrideSoundDirections(
            new SoundDirections(true, false, true, true),
            OverrideScope.UNTIL_IGNITION_OFF);
} catch (OverrideConflictException e) {
    ctx.log().warn("another plugin holds the parking override: " + e.getMessage());
}
Rule Value Permission vehicle.parking.write Conflict Only one plugin may hold the override; the second gets OverrideConflictException Scope UNTIL_IGNITION_OFF or PERSISTENT Restore The SDK's ledger restores the previous value when the plugin is disabled, quarantined, uninstalled, or the ignition goes off (for UNTIL_IGNITION_OFF)

The override is restored automatically. You can release it earlier:

override.release();

PERSISTENT overrides survive a reboot and are re-claimed by the plugin when it starts again. Use it only for a setting that should outlive the ignition cycle.

The ledger stores pending restores in /mnt/persist/mibsdk/ledger.properties and retries a failed restore with backoff. If the unit shuts down while an override is active, the next boot restores it before plugins load.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
ctx.events().on(IgnitionChanged.class, e -> {
    ctx.log().info("ignition " + (e.isOn() ? "on" : "off"));
});

ctx.events().on(ParkingSoundChanged.class, e -> {
    SoundDirections value = e.value();
});

ctx.events().on(TrailerHitchedChanged.class, e -> {
    boolean hitched = e.isHitched();
});
Event When IgnitionChanged Terminal 15 changes ParkingSoundChanged The parking-sound directions change TrailerHitchedChanged A trailer is hitched or unhitched HookObserved A hook point saw a value (needs hooks.parking)

Events are delivered after the fact, asynchronously, on the plugin's worker thread. They are not a way to veto or modify the stock behaviour; use hooks for that.

Listeners are cancelled when the plugin is disabled. on returns a Subscription if you want to stop one earlier.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text:
Hooks are declarative: you register a veto or an observation, and the stock side reads it. Plugin code never runs on a stock thread.

Veto veto = ctx.hooks().veto(HookPoint.PARKING_SOUND_SET);
veto.setActive(true);
...
veto.release();

ctx.hooks().observe(HookPoint.PARKING_SOUND_UPDATE, observed -> {
    SoundDirections value = (SoundDirections) observed.value();
    boolean wasVetoed = observed.vetoed();
});
Point Meaning PARKING_SOUND_SET A parking-sound value is about to be applied PARKING_SOUND_UPDATE A parking-sound value was observed

Hooks need the hooks.parking permission and Features.HOOK_PARKING. Without the feature, registration throws UnsupportedOperationException.

A veto is a flag, not a callback: it blocks the stock behaviour while active. release() clears it; the SDK also releases it when the plugin is disabled.

docs.title: What is not available
docs.text:
• No arbitrary stock method hooks. Only the hook points above.
  • No direct DSI or stock HMI classes. The plugin class loader hides them.
  • No raw sockets. Use ctx.net() for TCP queries (loopback by default, outbound with network.outbound).
  • No custom drawing or MENU-ring entries.

docs.title: API levels
docs.text:
The "api" field in plugin.json is the newest plugin API your code uses. It is not the SDK version and not your plugin version.

mibsdk.api.SdkInfo.API_VERSION is the newest level the SDK implements; MIN_API_VERSION is the oldest it still loads.

API Arrived in What it added 1 SDK 0.1.0 MibPlugin, PluginContext, Log, Storage, Scheduler, Events, Hooks, Vehicle/Parking, Permissions, Features 2 SDK 0.1.0 Ui.page, PageSpec (item, toggle, info, link), Page, UiAction, Ui.carMenuRow, Ui.statusItem/StatusItem, Net 3 SDK 0.2.0 Manifest "icons", Ui.icon, Ui.stockIcon, StockIcons, icon overloads of carMenuRow, statusItem and StatusItem.set 4 SDK 0.2.0 Ui.icon(name, colour) with Icon.TINTED / Icon.OWN_COLOURS 5 SDK 0.3.0 PageSpec.choice, dropdown, slider, progress, item icons, enabled; UiAction.value() / text(); Ui.confirm, Ui.toast, Ui.speller; Features.UI_INPUTS 6 SDK 0.3.0 StatusItem.setColour, StatusItem.visibleIn, StatusItem.setIcon; UiColor; HmiContext 7 SDK 0.6.2 ctx.wifi() with Wifi, WifiStatus, WifiNetwork, WifiChanged; Ui.textInput; Features.WIFI; network.wifi

The current SDK implements api 1–7.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
Levels are additive. A newer SDK runs older plugins unchanged. SDK 0.6.2 loads api 1–7.

Declare the lowest level that covers what you use. The build enforces it: a call to an api 5 member while the manifest declares api 4 fails with the call site:

permissionScan: ...CoffeeTimerPlugin.spec -> PageSpec.slider needs api 5; plugin.json declares api 4

Compile-time constants such as PageSpec.MAX_OPTIONS are inlined by the compiler, so they leave no call site and are not checked.

mibpkg checks the range. It installs a plugin only when sdk.min_api <= plugin.api <= sdk.api for the SDK on the unit. An api-7 plugin needs SDK 0.6.2 or later.

Features are separate. An api level says what the API has. ctx.has(Features.X) says what this unit can draw at this boot. A missing feature makes the matching handle inert, not failing. Check the feature when the difference matters.

docs.title: Choosing a level
docs.text: If you use Declare Only lifecycle, storage, timers, events, vehicle 1 Any page, Car row, status item or network query 2 Your own PNG icons or a built-in icon 3 Icon.OWN_COLOURS 4 A slider, dropdown, choice, progress, toast, confirm or speller 5 Status-item colour, per-context visibility or icon-only items 6 The Wi-Fi uplink or a masked text field 7

docs.text: The generated Java API reference is the exact contract. This page is the map: which type to reach for and how the pieces fit together.

docs.title: The entry point
docs.text:
public class MyPlugin extends MibPlugin {
    @Override
    protected void onEnable(PluginContext ctx) {
        // everything starts here
    }
}

docs.text:
• Everything in mibsdk.api is compiled against by plugins.
  • mibsdk.runtime, mibsdk.platform and mibsdk.adapter.hqc are internal and hidden at runtime.
  • The test harness and fake car are host-only and never ship to the unit.

docs.title: Plugin tasks
docs.text:
The mibsdk.plugin convention adds these tasks to your project:

Task Output What it does mibPluginJar build/mibsdk/<id>.jar and .jar.stamp Compiles, backports, checks and packs the plugin mibpkgPackage build/mibsdk/<id>-<version>.mpk Stages the jar, stamp, icons and manifest.toml, then runs the host mibpkg mibpkgPackageStage build/mibpkg-stage/ Stages the package contents without packing test Test reports Runs host tests on the real runtime and fake car backport build/v48/ Lowers class files to v48 classVersionCheck report Every class is v48 linkCheck build/reports/mibsdk/linkcheck.txt Every reference resolves against the car class library permissionScan build/reports/mibsdk/permissions.txt Permissions, api level, reflection/exec mibPackage — Deprecated alias for mibpkgPackage

The normal commands:

./gradlew test
./gradlew mibPluginJar
./gradlew mibpkgPackage
./gradlew build          # assemble + check

mibPluginJar depends on classVersionCheck, linkCheck and permissionScan. A failure in any of them fails the jar.

docs.title: Build properties
docs.text:
Set these with -P or in $GRADLE_USER_HOME/gradle.properties:

Property Used by Meaning mibsdk.repo Plugin settings The Maven repository that holds the SDK artifacts. Empty means the published repository mibsdk.mibpkg mibpkgPackage The host mibpkg binary. Default: mibpkg on PATH mibsdk.jdk8Home backport, compat A JDK 8 home. Default: the Gradle toolchain's JDK 8 mibsdk.stockLsdJar SDK maintainers jxe2jar's lsd.jar. Not needed for a plugin build mibsdk.stockDsiTracerJar SDK maintainers The stock DSITracer.jar. Not needed for a plugin build

A property that points at a missing file fails with a message that names the property. There are no machine-specific defaults under your home directory.

From a checkout of this repository:

docs.title: mibsdk-dev
docs.text:
installer/mibsdk-dev is a bash wrapper around the unit's mibpkg, run from your computer over SSH. It uploads files to /tmp, passes mibpkg's output and exit code through, and never reads the j9 command line (which embeds the VIN and IMSI).

usage: mibsdk-dev <command> [args] [host]      (host: the last argument, else $MIBSDK_HOST)

There is no default host.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Command What it does install Upload and install the SDK package (dist/build/dist/mibsdk-*.mpk, or $MIBSDK_MPK) uninstall [--purge] [--force] Remove the SDK. --purge deletes plugin data; --force uninstalls while overrides are active install-plugin <file.mpk> [--approve=<perm,...>] Install or update a plugin package remove <id> [--purge\|--purge-data] Remove a plugin; keeps data unless purged push <plugin.jar> Upload a jar and its stamp, then reload the plugin grant <id> <perm,...> Grant permissions; an empty list revokes all safe-mode on\|off Force safe mode on or off; off also resets the boot counter boot-state set-wrap <n> Set the boot-guard wrap count data-clear <id> Delete a plugin's storage; restart afterwards to free the quota status The SDK, plugins, states, grants, ledger and STATUS lines log Print /tmp/mibsdk.log restart Restart the HMI (a bench reset takes 2–3 minutes) ui-forcefail factory\|screen\|off Developer switch to make the SDK UI fail on purpose; read at boot

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
mibsdk-dev passes mibpkg's status through:

Code Meaning 0 Success 1 Failed or busy 2 Bad usage 3 Permissions need approval; re-run with --approve=...

docs.title: Environment
docs.text: Variable Meaning MIBSDK_HOST The unit address when it is not the last argument MIBSDK_DIST The dist directory (default dist/build/dist) MIBSDK_MPK The SDK package to install

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
installer/mibsdk-dev status 10.0.0.5
installer/mibsdk-dev log 10.0.0.5
installer/mibsdk-dev push build/mibsdk/coffee-timer.jar 10.0.0.5
installer/mibsdk-dev grant coffee-timer ui.slot.carmenu,ui.slot.statusbar 10.0.0.5
installer/mibsdk-dev safe-mode on 10.0.0.5

docs.title: SSH details
docs.text:
The unit uses an old RSA host key. The tool passes:

-o HostKeyAlgorithms=ssh-rsa -o PubkeyAcceptedKeyTypes=ssh-rsa
-o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=8

It logs in as root. Key-based auth must already work.

docs.title: Java compatibility
docs.text: The car runs IBM J9 2.3 with a Java 1.4 class library and loads only class-file version 48. You write modern Java; the build lowers it for you. Modern syntax is fine. Modern library calls are not.

docs.title: Syntax you can use
docs.text:
• lambdas and method references;
  • var;
  • switch expressions and arrow switches;
  • text blocks;
  • enhanced for;
  • generics;
  • autoboxing;
  • try-with-resources;
  • Java 8+ annotations that Jabel understands.

The build compiles with JDK 17 and --release 8, then runs Retrolambda and Retrotranslator.

docs.title: Records are not supported
docs.text:
A record fails in compileJava with Jabel's message:

error: Must be annotated with @Desugar

Use a final class with final fields instead.

docs.title: The car's class library is old
docs.text:
Retrotranslator backports some Java 5 API, including StringBuilder, Integer.valueOf and String.format. The compat module supplies shims for:

  • Objects;
  • AutoCloseable;
  • Function, Consumer, Supplier, Predicate, BiFunction, BinaryOperator, UnaryOperator, BiConsumer, BiPredicate;
  • IntFunction, IntPredicate, IntUnaryOperator, ToIntFunction, IntSupplier, BooleanSupplier.

The numeric and Long/Double variants of the rest are missing.

docs.title: What linkCheck rejects
docs.text:
linkCheck compares every reference against a signature list of the car's class library and fails with the reference and its call site:

> LinkCheck: 1 reference(s) the car cannot resolve:
    member java/lang/String.matches(Ljava/lang/String;)Z
      used by tutorial/coffeetimer/CoffeeTimerPlugin.start
      hint: no regex on the car: use indexOf/substring or a loop

Known gaps:

Missing Use instead java.util.regex, String.matches, split, replaceAll indexOf, substring, a loop String.join StringBuilder java.util.concurrent ctx.scheduler() and the one-worker model; synchronized if needed java.time store millis; System.currentTimeMillis() Streams (List.stream()) loops

If you use a class that Retrotranslator rewrote, the report also names the class you wrote, in parentheses, so you can find the import to remove.

docs.title: No reflection or escape routes
docs.text:
The build rejects these unless you declare platform.unrestricted:

  • Class.forName, Method.invoke, Constructor.newInstance;
  • Runtime.exec, System.exit, native loading, Thread.stop;
  • raw Socket, ServerSocket, URL.openConnection, InetAddress.getByName.

Use ctx.net() for TCP queries.

docs.title: No stock classes
docs.text:
Your class loader sees only:

  • java.*
  • javax.*
  • mibsdk.api.*
  • mibsdk.compat.*
  • net.sf.retrotranslator.runtime.*

The manufacturer's stock packages and mibsdk.runtime.* are hidden. You cannot patch or call the stock HMI. Changes to stock behaviour go through declarative hooks.

docs.title: Threads
docs.text:
All plugin code runs on one SDK-owned worker thread per plugin, one task at a time. Do not block it:

  • no Thread.sleep loops;
  • no long I/O; ctx.net().query is capped at 3 s;
  • use ctx.scheduler() for periodic or delayed work.

You can start your own thread; the build does not stop you. Do not: the SDK cannot cancel or quarantine work on it, and it keeps running after the plugin is disabled.

docs.title: Kotlin
docs.text: Kotlin works. Apply id("org.jetbrains.kotlin.jvm") before id("mibsdk.plugin"). The convention sets the Kotlin target to 1.8 and runs a shrink step before the backport. The mib2q-plugins monorepo's bike-rack sample is the reference.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Permissions make a plugin's intent visible and stop accidents. They are a seat belt, not a sandbox: they do not stop a plugin that sets out to do harm.

docs.title: The catalog
docs.text:
Permission Grants Approval text vehicle.read ctx.vehicle() and parking state Read vehicle state: ignition, gear, parking sensors vehicle.parking.write Parking.overrideSoundDirections Change parking-sensor settings, for example mute the rear tones hooks.parking ctx.hooks() and HookObserved events Watch and override parking-system messages ui.slot.carmenu Ui.carMenuRow Add a row to the Car menu ui.slot.statusbar Ui.statusItem, Ui.toast Show an item in the status bar network ctx.net() for loopback Query local services on this unit (loopback only) network.outbound ctx.net() for non-loopback hosts Connect to hosts outside this unit network.wifi ctx.wifi() Use the Wi-Fi client uplink to connect to a phone hotspot or another network platform.unrestricted Reflection, raw sockets, stock classes Unrestricted: may use reflection and stock HMI classes; the SDK cannot contain it

The source of truth is api/permissions.json.

docs.title: Declared and granted
docs.text:
A permission must be both declared and granted:

  1. The plugin declares it in plugin.json "permissions".
  2. The user approves it at install time.
  3. The runtime exposes the matching API only when both are true.

If any declared permission is not granted, the plugin is BLOCKED_PERMISSIONS and does not start. There are no optional permissions yet.

A granted but undeclared permission is unusable: the build refuses the call, and the runtime reports permission not declared in plugin.json if one slips through.

docs.title: Build-time enforcement
docs.text:
permissionScan knows which API members need which permission and fails the build when you call one without declaring it:

tutorial/coffeetimer/CoffeeTimerPlugin.onEnable -> Ui.carMenuRow needs "ui.slot.carmenu":
declare it in plugin.json "permissions"

A call inside if (ctx.granted(...)) still needs the declaration. Declaring platform.unrestricted does not excuse it.

docs.title: Runtime enforcement
docs.text:
The API checks the grant when you call it. A missing grant throws PermissionDeniedException (a RuntimeException) with permission() naming the permission. Normally a plugin with a missing grant never reaches this point because it is blocked at load.

Revoking a permission stops the plugin: it becomes BLOCKED_PERMISSIONS until the permission is granted again.

docs.title: platform.unrestricted
docs.text:
This is the loud escape hatch. It lifts the build's ban on:

  • Class.forName, Method.invoke, Constructor.newInstance;
  • Runtime.exec, System.exit, native loading, Thread.stop;
  • raw Socket, ServerSocket, URL.openConnection, InetAddress.getByName.

mibpkg shows a danger warning at install, and the SDK cannot contain the plugin. Use it only for a plugin you control and do not intend to share.

docs.title: Checking grants from code
docs.text:
if (ctx.granted(Permissions.NETWORK)) {
    // ...
}

ctx.has(Features.X) is different: it says what this unit can do at this boot, not what the user approved.

docs.title: plugin.json
docs.text:
Every plugin has src/main/resources/plugin.json. The build reads it for packaging and checks; the runtime reads the copy at the jar root.

{
  "id": "coffee-timer",
  "name": "Coffee Timer",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "author": "your-name",
  "api": 5,
  "main": "tutorial.coffeetimer.CoffeeTimerPlugin",
  "permissions": ["ui.slot.carmenu", "ui.slot.statusbar"],
  "icons": ["cup", "cup-20"]
}

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Required Rules id Yes 2–40 characters: a letter, then a-z, 0-9 and -. It names the jar, the mibpkg package, your storage and your icon directory. mibsdk is reserved name Yes Free text shown in the Plugins menu and in mibpkg version Yes Semver: 1.2.3 or 1.2.3-beta.1. mibpkg uses it to order updates author Yes Free text. Read by the runtime; ignored by the build api Yes Integer 1–7: the newest plugin API your code uses main Yes Fully qualified class that extends mibsdk.api.MibPlugin permissions No Array of permission ids from api/permissions.json icons No Array of icon names, [a-z0-9-]{1,32}, at most 8. Needs "api": 3 or higher. Each needs src/main/icons/<name>.png dependencies No Array of plugin ids that must be enabled first. Read by the runtime; not checked by the build

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
PluginJson.read fails the build for:

  • missing id, name, version, main;
  • an id outside the rule above, or mibsdk;
  • a version that is not semver;
  • an api outside 1–7, or a non-integer;
  • an unknown permission, with a "did you mean" hint;
  • an invalid, duplicate or excessive icon name;
  • "icons" with an api below 3;
  • a missing icon PNG, or a PNG that fails the format rules.

permissionScan additionally fails the build when:

  • your code uses a permission the manifest does not declare;
  • your code uses API newer than "api";
  • your code uses reflection, exec or raw sockets without platform.unrestricted.

It warns when a status-bar call names a declared icon larger than 20×20.

docs.title: Runtime
docs.text:
ManifestParser re-checks the manifest when the jar is loaded. A plugin whose manifest is invalid is BLOCKED_INVALID. A plugin whose declared permissions are not all granted is BLOCKED_PERMISSIONS and never starts.

The runtime accepts a slightly wider id range than the build (2–41 characters, starting with a letter or digit). Use the build's rule; it is the one that determines whether a package can be created.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
The catalog lives in api/permissions.json:

Id Approval text vehicle.read Read vehicle state: ignition, gear, parking sensors vehicle.parking.write Change parking-sensor settings, for example mute the rear tones hooks.parking Watch and override parking-system messages ui.slot.carmenu Add a row to the Car menu ui.slot.statusbar Show an item in the status bar network Query local services on this unit (loopback only) network.outbound Connect to hosts outside this unit platform.unrestricted Unrestricted: may use reflection and stock HMI classes; the SDK cannot contain it

See Permissions for the enforcement model.

docs.text:
"icons" lists file names without the .png extension:

src/main/icons/cup.png      declared as "cup"
src/main/icons/cup-20.png   declared as "cup-20"

The package carries them as icons/<name>.png; mibpkg installs them as icons/<id>/<sha16>.png.

docs.title: First checks
docs.text:
1. installer/mibsdk-dev status <unit-ip> — is the plugin ENABLED?
  2. installer/mibsdk-dev log <unit-ip> — what is the last STATUS or ERROR line?
  3. Does the same plugin pass ./gradlew test on the host?
  4. Is the SDK itself running, or is the unit in safe mode?

docs.title: Plugin states
docs.text: State Cause Fix BLOCKED_INVALID Unreadable jar, invalid plugin.json, or jar not named <id>.jar Rebuild with mibPluginJar; check the manifest BLOCKED_PERMISSIONS A declared permission is not granted Approve the full list, or mibsdk-dev grant BLOCKED_DEPENDENCY A "dependencies" entry is missing, blocked, disabled or cyclic Fix the dependency FAILED Loading the class or onEnable threw Read the log; fix and push QUARANTINED 3 failures in 60 s or a 30 s hang Fix and push; a reload re-enables it DISABLED Switched off in the Plugins menu or by a reload Re-enable it

docs.title: permission not declared in plugin.json: X
docs.text: Your code calls an API that needs X and the manifest does not declare it. Add X to "permissions". Granting it on the unit does not help: an undeclared permission can never be used.

docs.title: permission not granted: X
docs.text: The manifest declares X but the user has not approved it. Install with approval or grant it. Normally the plugin is BLOCKED_PERMISSIONS before it gets this far.

docs.title: ... needs api 5; plugin.json declares api 4
docs.text: Raise "api" to the level the call needs. The error names the call site. See API levels.

docs.title: reference(s) the car cannot resolve
docs.text: linkCheck names the missing class or member, the call site and usually a hint. Common causes: java.util.regex, String.join, java.util.concurrent, streams, java.time. See Java compatibility.

docs.title: 1 call(s) need platform.unrestricted
docs.text: You used reflection, exec, native loading or a raw socket. Use ctx.net() for TCP, or declare platform.unrestricted if you really need the escape hatch.

docs.title: main class ... is not among the plugin's classes
docs.text: "main" in plugin.json does not match the class you wrote, or the package is wrong.

docs.title: icon 'x' is declared in plugin.json but src/main/icons/x.png does not exist
docs.text: Add the file or remove the name from "icons".

docs.title: icon ... must be 8-bit RGBA / at most 72 px / 32 KiB
docs.text: Re-export the PNG with those properties. Palette PNGs and interlaced PNGs are rejected.

docs.title: parent directory ... does not exist / wrapper errors
docs.text: You copied the project without the gradle/wrapper directory. Copy the whole templates/plugin tree, or run gradle wrapper.

docs.title: mibsdk.repo is not set
docs.text:
The template's gradle.properties has an empty mibsdk.repo, which means "use the published repository". If you are offline or testing a local SDK build, set it to a checkout's build/repo:

mibsdk.repo=file:///absolute/path/to/mib2q-plugin-sdk/build/repo

docs.title: Plugin [id: 'mibsdk.plugin', version: '...'] was not found
docs.text: The repository URL does not contain that plugin version, or mibsdk.repo points at the wrong checkout. Publish the SDK with ./gradlew publishLocal, and make the version in build.gradle.kts match mibsdk.version.

docs.title: mibsdk: mibsdk.mibpkg is not set
docs.text: mibpkgPackage needs the host binary. Build it with cargo build --release in the mibpkg repository and set mibsdk.mibpkg, or put mibpkg on PATH.

docs.title: A status icon is too large
docs.text: a status icon is at most 20x20 px, this one is 72x72 — use a 20 px icon for statusItem and toast.

docs.title: A toggle does not stick
docs.text: The HMI does not flip a checkbox by itself. Store the requested value and call page.update(spec()).

docs.title: A blank row icon after a push
docs.text: Icons arrive only with a package. Install the .mpk.

docs.title: A row or page does not appear
docs.text:
• The feature may be missing this boot: check ctx.has(Features.UI_PAGES), Features.SLOT_CAR_MENU, Features.SLOT_STATUS_BAR.
  • The Car screen reads its rows when it opens; reopen it after changing a row.
  • A plugin with a missing grant never starts.

docs.title: The plugin is quarantined
docs.text: Three callback failures in 60 s, or a callback still running after 30 s. The log names the failure. Fix the exception or split the slow work; then push or reload.

docs.title: The unit boots in safe mode
docs.text: Three unhealthy boots in a row. The SDK runs with no plugins and restores pending overrides. Use mibsdk-dev safe-mode off after fixing the plugin, and inspect the log from the previous boot.

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text:
installer/mibsdk-dev status <unit-ip>
installer/mibsdk-dev log <unit-ip>
installer/mibsdk-dev data-clear <id> <unit-ip>   # corrupted storage
installer/mibsdk-dev remove <id> <unit-ip>       # then reinstall

In a host test, h.await prints the pages and the runtime log when it fails. h.log() returns the log.

docs.title: Still stuck?
docs.text:
Open an issue with:

  • the HMI build from /ifs/version_info.txt;
  • the SDK version;
  • the plugin's plugin.json and the failing code;
  • the relevant log lines (remove VIN, IMSI and location first).
